assets.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create a new square editorial lifestyle photograph for the Compact pocket-mirror iPhone app website. A fictional adult woman getting ready to go out to dinner, seated at a small dressing table, applying a light touch of blush to her cheek with a soft makeup brush. Elegant everyday evening outfit, shoulder-length chestnut hair, natural skin texture, tasteful cream apartment, warm evening light, understated candid photography.
SIMPLE PHYSICALLY PLAUSIBLE COMPOSITION: the iPhone stands UPRIGHT on a small believable tabletop phone stand in front of her. NOBODY is holding the phone. Her LEFT hand and LEFT forearm rest in her lap completely outside the crop. Exactly ONE hand is visible: her anatomical RIGHT hand gently holding a makeup brush with its bristles touching her right cheek. Show one continuous relaxed wrist and forearm leading from her right shoulder to that right hand; natural finger lengths and a normal brush grip. Her arm is raised comfortably, with no crossed arms, duplicated hands or extra limb. Compose a medium close three-quarter side view from just behind her left shoulder, so the face, the brushing gesture and the phone screen are all legible. Do not expose hidden limbs just to display them.
The phone is close enough to use as a mirror, and her eyes are directed naturally toward its display. Its screen shows the corresponding mirrored front-camera view of this same woman, same expression, same brush touching the same cheek, with realistic perspective. Keep the displayed reflection simple and small enough to be natural. The Compact app UI is subtle: a small round gear in the upper-left corner and three separate small dark translucent round bottom controls showing a sun, '1×', and viewfinder corners. No camera shutter, recording indicator, captions, promotional text, logos or watermarks.
One woman, ONE visible real hand, one brush, one phone on a stand. A few softly blurred cosmetic objects on the dressing table are fine. The main subject and phone should read clearly in a square landing-page card.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: existing Compact mirror landing-page lifestyle photograph. Edit target: supplied square photograph of a woman applying lipstick while viewing her phone. Relax the wrist into a comfortable lipstick-applying pose while keeping the lipstick tip at her lips. Keep five anatomically coherent fingers with a natural grip. Update only the corresponding hand/lipstick reflection on the phone to agree with this minor correction. Preserve the woman's identity, face, hair, hoop earring, skin, black top, left hand holding the phone, exact phone placement and Compact UI, warm sunset lighting, apartment background, square crop, camera viewpoint and overall composition. Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: the supplied original square Compact lifestyle photograph. Correct ONLY the foreground RIGHT hand holding lipstick, to the right of the phone. Rotate that hand COUNTERCLOCKWISE (anticlockwise) by about 15–20 degrees as seen by the viewer, with the fingertips leaning further LEFT relative to the wrist. The previous attempt went clockwise; the user explicitly wants the OPPOSITE direction. Keep the wrist relaxed and anatomically connected to the forearm, with a natural five-finger grip. Keep the lipstick touching her lips and make the smallest necessary wrist/forearm adjustment to accommodate this anticlockwise rotation. Match the small hand/lipstick change in the phone reflection. Preserve everything else: same woman, identity, face, hair, hoop earring, black top, left hand holding phone, phone position, Compact UI, square crop, warm light, apartment background and camera viewpoint. Do not rotate the whole image. Do not create a new scene or change her overall pose.

Edit only the right hand holding the lipstick in this photograph. Change its orientation in 3D by roughly a quarter turn around the forearm axis: the PALM must face the camera and slightly to image LEFT, while the BACK OF THE HAND and its outer knuckles face image RIGHT toward the woman's cheek and are hidden on the far side. Make the palm's creases, soft inner finger pads and inner wrist visibly face us. We must NOT see the broad smooth dorsal back of the hand, a row of outside knuckles, or the fingernails of the curled fingers. The thumb and index finger hold the lipstick in a relaxed light pinch, the remaining fingers curl loosely, and the lipstick tip remains touching her lips. Exactly one anatomically correct right hand and one continuous wrist/forearm. This is a palm-versus-back orientation correction, not a 2D tilt or merely moving the hand sideways. Match the changed hand orientation in the phone reflection. Keep every other part of the supplied image unchanged, including the woman's identity, face, hair, clothes, phone-holding left hand, phone position, phone UI, room, warm lighting, viewpoint and square crop.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this existing Compact lifestyle photograph. Preserve the current position and orientation of the woman's RIGHT wrist/forearm: the inner wrist and palm side face the viewer, and the outside knuckles face away to image right. Make TWO closely related corrections only.
1. NATURAL LIPSTICK GRIP: Replace the delicate fingertip pinch at the gold collar with an ordinary practical makeup grip LOWER DOWN around the BLACK BASE of the lipstick tube. Her thumb pad and the sides/pads of her gently bent index and middle fingers hold the black barrel securely, like someone actually applying lipstick. The ring and little fingers curl loosely into the palm. The tube sits within the grip, not balanced between extended fingertips. No fingers pinch the gold collar or the lipstick bullet. Keep a relaxed wrist, five anatomically correct fingers, natural finger lengths, and lipstick tip touching the lower lip. Preserve the currently improved inward-facing hand orientation; do not show the broad outside knuckles toward the viewer.
2. MATCH THE PHONE REFLECTION PHYSICALLY: The display must show this exact same grip and lipstick application from the front-camera's OPPOSITE viewpoint, with normal mirrored-preview handedness. Because the real foreground hand shows its palm/inner side to us, the PHONE must show the corresponding BACK/OUTER side of that same hand and fingers, not another copy of the palm-facing view. On the phone, the hand rises from the lower right of the screen holding the same black-and-gold tube lower on its black base; the tip touches the same point on her lower lip. Match the finger arrangement, wrist angle, tube angle and scale between the two views. Only one lipstick hand is present in each view. The on-screen hand should naturally occlude a little of the lower cheek/chin, with correct perspective.
Preserve everything else exactly: woman's identity, face and expression, hair, earrings, black top, left hand holding phone, phone angle and placement, Compact controls, warm apartment setting, lighting and square crop. Do not replace the scene or change her overall pose.

Local photographic inpainting: completely REMOVE AND REDRAW the foreground lipstick-holding hand and its wrist. Do not preserve its existing fingers or thumb; their left-handed anatomy is wrong. Leave the phone-holding left hand untouched.
Draw her anatomical RIGHT HAND holding lipstick to her mouth, seen from the PALM side, with a relaxed grip around the black barrel. For this palm-facing RIGHT hand, place the THUMB unmistakably on the IMAGE-LEFT / PHONE-facing side, and the FOUR FINGERS on the IMAGE-RIGHT / FACE-facing side. The thumb pad presses the left side of the black tube, while index and middle fingers curl around from the right side; ring and little fingers curl below. The thumb's short broad tip stays LEFT of the four fingers. Do not put a tall thumb with a prominent nail on the right or in front as in the input. Show palm creases and a natural right wrist; hide the outer knuckles on the right. This must look like one left hand holding a phone and one right hand applying lipstick. Keep the lipstick tip on the lower lip. Reconstruct this region from scratch, with realistic human anatomy, not by tweaking or rotating the incorrect input hand.
Also correct the lipstick hand visible on the PHONE: it must be the matching mirrored live-camera view of the SAME RIGHT hand from the opposite side, matching the grip and lipstick angle. Keep its existing face and app buttons.
Everything outside the lipstick hand/wrist region and the matching small phone reflection edit must remain unchanged: same woman, phone, clothing, left hand, warm apartment, light, composition, square crop. Do not change the framing.

Edit only the foreground lipstick-holding hand and its matching image on the phone. Follow this explicit visual requirement: as WE VIEW THIS PHOTO, the lipstick hand's THUMB is on the FAR RIGHT of the hand, closest to the woman's cheek. The FOUR FINGERS are to its LEFT, toward the phone. The previous version put the thumb on the left; remove that wrong left-side thumb completely and rebuild the grip. Do not preserve that anatomy.
The thumb must emerge from the right-hand edge of the palm/wrist, curve upward along the hand's far-right outline, and press the RIGHT side of the BLACK lipstick barrel. It is the rightmost visible digit. The index and middle fingers curl from the LEFT around the opposite side of the barrel, while ring and little fingers curl below on the left. Use a short broad two-segment thumb, four distinct natural fingers, five digits total, a relaxed wrist, and an ordinary practical lipstick grip. Keep the lipstick tip touching her lower lip. Keep the inner side of the hand visible and avoid displaying a row of outside knuckles toward the camera. Rebuild the hand rather than simply tilting the current wrong grip. The required visible result is THUMB FAR RIGHT, FOUR FINGERS LEFT.
Update the phone's mirrored front-camera view to show the corresponding opposite viewpoint of this same hand, grip, lipstick angle and point of contact with the lip. Do not duplicate the foreground view on the screen.
Preserve everything else: the phone-holding hand, face, expression, hair, earrings, black top, shoulders, phone placement and controls, apartment, warm sunset lighting, square crop and camera viewpoint. No extra limbs, no new objects, no whole-image rotation.
